newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Seven says to spend A$62.5 mln on Optus.
newsitem.headline: Seven says to spend A$62.5 mln on Optus.

text.p: Seven Network Ltd said on Friday it will spend A$62.5 million to acquire an equity holding in telecommunications carrier Optus Communications Ltd.
The expenditure is linked to an agreement reached on Friday transferring 100 percent ownership of pay television and telephone company Optus Vision to Optus Communications.

Seven said it will initially acquire the rights to 50 million shares in Optus Communications at A$1.25 a share, with an entitlement to acquire an additional 50 million shares when the company is listed on the Australian Stock Exchange at the float price.

Current shareholders in Optus Vision are Optus Communications and Continental Cablevision Inc, owned by American telephone concern US West Inc, with 46.5 percent each, Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd at five percent and Seven Network at two percent.
As a result of the acquisition, Seven will transfer its interest in Optus Vision to Optus Communications," Seven said.
"Seven's investment in Optus Communications makes sound business sense," Seven chairman Kerry Stokes said in a statement.
"We believe the company is well managed and strategically placed to play a vital role in the development of communications technologies in Australia," he said.
Seven said it will continue to play a pivotal role in the future development of Optus Vision through its interest in Optus Vision's programming and channel ventures.
Seven said it will maintain its 30 percent stake in Sportsvision and is committed to suppling it with programming.
The company also said it will retain its 8.33 percent shareholding in MovieVision.

The investment in Optus Communications underlines a long-term strategy at Seven on strengthening its involvement in entertainment software and the identification of long-term partnerships to secure a major presence in delivery platforms for the software, Seven said.
As part of the agreement, Seven dropped legal actions against the other parties to Optus Vision.
"Seven's pursuit of legal action was an indication of the company's resolve to ensure the protection of its business interests and indeed the interests of all its shareholders," Stokes said.
Seven had been suing other shareholders for alleged breaches last August in the Optus Vision shareholders' agreement.

Seven claimed Optus Communications, US West and Publishing and Broadcasting were breaching the shareholders' agreement when they agreed to grant options which would increase Publishing and Broadcasting's stake in Optus Vision.
